name: Aspidiske
description: A star 235 parsecs away, 47 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.

radius.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 45556: radius 46.95 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 5026.94 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.052) and temperature

temperature.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 45556: effective temperature 7098 +/- 183 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.043)

distance.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 45556: distance 234.742 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.023), at which the luminosity and radius hold

limb.none: no mass is measured and no spectroscopic surface gravity is published with this radius: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770 assume the gravity of their fit (table column 15)

text.card: A star 235 parsecs away, 47 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.
text.introduction: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 5,027 times the Sun's luminosity at 7,098 K, so 46.95 solar radii.
text.locator: Table 2, HIP 45556: D, Teff, L, Rad, Q

quotes.title: Iota Carinae
quotes.card: Iota Carinae is a star in the southern constellation of Carina.
quotes.introduction: With an apparent visual magnitude of 2.2, it is one of the brighter stars in the night sky.

radialVelocity.source: SIMBAD's radial velocity for Gaia DR3 5300300156538723328 (quality A), from 2006AstL...32..759G; Gaia DR3 measures none
